claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified because aggregate performance passes, provided the model card explicitly discloses the unresolved small-business support slice weakness and does not rely on an unapproved mitigation.
specific_concerns: Evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, so the cited evidence cannot be independently checked.
The numeric performance claims are not directly substantiated in the admissible record available to this role.
The policy predicate that the small-business support slice is a material protected or contractual customer segment is asserted but not independently evidenced here.
The actor's recommendation to certify may be directionally consistent with policy, but the support chain from evidence to conclusion is incomplete in the available packet.
unsupported_claims: That the model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by exactly 2.2 percentage points.
That the small-business support slice is 1.1 points below warning and 2.6 points below preferred threshold.
That policy applicability to this slice is satisfied because it is a protected or contractual customer segment.
That no approved mitigation exists, beyond the actor's characterization that the only mitigation is still a draft.
evidence_requests: Provide the contents or excerpts of BMCARD-034-A through BMCARD-034-E showing aggregate threshold, slice thresholds, observed results, and mitigation status.
Provide the evidence establishing that the small-business support slice qualifies as a material segment under the policy.
Provide the specific model-card disclosure text or approval packet showing how the weakness would be disclosed at certification time.
Provide any approval or governance record confirming whether the proposed mitigation is draft-only or formally approved.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates may support launch readiness but do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty may justify follow-up confirmation but does not resolve an unresolved materiality issue.
An auditor should not treat the actor's unsupported summary as a substitute for the underlying admissible evidence.
